title: How to Clean Florida Pollen Stains Off Siding
description: Oak and pine pollen can bake into Florida siding. Learn how to soft wash it off safely, what to avoid, and how to keep the yellow film from returning.
excerpt: Yellow pollen film can bake into painted siding. Here is how to soft wash it off safely and time your rinses so it never sets.
h1: How to Clean Florida Pollen Stains Off Your Home's Exterior
heroIntro: Spring pollen in North Central Florida does more than coat your car. Left on painted siding through a few dew-and-sun cycles, it sets into a stubborn yellow-green stain that a garden hose will not touch.

sections.h2: Why pollen turns into a stain instead of washing away
body: Fresh pollen is just loose dust. The trouble starts when it sits. Live oaks, laurel oaks, and pines release heavy loads of pollen from late winter through spring, and in our area that coincides with cool, dewy mornings and warm afternoons. Every morning the dew wets the grains; every afternoon the sun dries them. After a week or two of that cycle, the oils and sugars in the pollen work into the texture of the paint film and leave a baked-on pollen stain that rain alone will not rinse.

Flat and satin finishes, textured stucco, and chalky older paint hold pollen the worst because they have more surface area for it to grip. Gloss trim and smooth vinyl usually come clean more easily. Pollen also feeds mildew: a wall that stays coated and damp in spring often turns gray-green by early summer, which is a separate problem covered in our guide to mold and mildew on siding.

sections.h2: Is it pollen, mildew, or chalking?
body: Before you choose a cleaner, identify what you are looking at. Each one responds to a different method.
bullets: Pollen: yellow to greenish-yellow, heaviest on horizontal ledges, window sills, and the windward side; smears into a yellow streak when rubbed with a damp cloth.
Mildew: gray, green, or black speckles, worst on shaded north walls and under eaves; a drop of diluted household bleach lightens it within a minute or two.
Chalking: the paint itself breaking down; a dry dark cloth rubbed on the wall comes away white or the color of the paint. Cleaning helps, but the wall is telling you a repaint is coming.

sections.h2: Step-by-step: soft washing pollen off siding and trim
body: The safe method is a low-pressure soft wash. High pressure is the wrong tool: it can force water behind lap siding and into window frames, etch soft wood, and gouge stucco texture.
bullets: Close windows, cover outlets and light fixtures, and soak nearby plants with plain water so they are less likely to absorb runoff.

Mix a house-wash detergent made for exterior painted surfaces according to its label. If you also see mildew, use a product formulated for both, and never mix bleach with ammonia-based or acidic cleaners.
Apply from the bottom up with a pump sprayer or a pressure washer on its soap/low-pressure setting, which keeps clean streaks from running down a dry, dirty wall.
Let the solution dwell for the time on the label, but do not let it dry on the surface. Work in shaded sections on hot days.
Scrub stubborn ledges and sills with a soft-bristle brush on an extension pole.
Rinse from the top down with plenty of low-pressure water, holding the nozzle level or angled down so you never drive water up under siding laps.
Rinse the plants again when you finish.

body: Vinyl and fiber cement clean up easily with a soft wash; avoid abrasive pads that dull the finish. Stucco needs a little more dwell time and gentle brushing, because pollen settles into the texture; keep the nozzle well back from the wall. Painted wood trim and fascia should never see a narrow, high-pressure tip, which raises the grain and can lift sound paint. Screens, pool enclosures, and window tracks collect huge amounts of pollen and are worth rinsing at the same time so they do not keep redepositing it on the walls.

If you are on a two-story home, the upper walls, gables, and soffits are where DIY washing gets risky. Working a wand from an extension ladder is unstable, and wet surfaces make it worse. That is often the point where homeowners hand the job to a professional soft washing crew with the right equipment for height.

sections.h2: Mistakes that make pollen stains worse
body: Most of the damage we see from pollen cleanup comes from the cleanup, not the pollen. A few habits to avoid:
bullets: Using a zero-degree or turbo nozzle on painted surfaces. It strips paint, scars wood, and blasts water into wall cavities.
Washing in full midday sun, which dries detergent into streaks that look worse than the pollen did.
Scrubbing with abrasive pads or stiff wire brushes, which burnish flat paint into shiny patches.
Using straight bleach, which can damage plants, corrode metal fixtures, and does little to pollen itself.
Spraying upward under siding laps, soffits, or window head trim, where water has no way to drain back out.
Skipping the rinse. Detergent left on the wall attracts dirt and can leave a dull film.

sections.h2: Timing your rinses so the film never sets
body: The cheapest fix is not letting pollen cure in the first place. A simple schedule works well in Alachua, Marion, and the surrounding counties: a late-March rinse once the heaviest oak drop is over, and a second wash in June before the summer storms and mildew take over. A plain water rinse with a garden hose in between, focused on sills, ledges, and the porch ceiling, keeps the load low.

Trim back limbs that hang over the roof and walls, keep gutters clear so pollen-laden water does not overflow down the siding, and wash before any planned painting. Paint applied over a pollen-dusted wall does not bond well, which is one of the quieter reasons exterior jobs fail early; we cover more of that in our North Central Florida exterior care guide.

sections.h2: When a cleaning becomes a painting conversation
body: If the wall is clean but still looks blotchy, if your cloth test shows heavy chalking, or if paint flakes come off with the rinse water, the coating has reached the end of its useful life. Washing will not restore it, and aggressive scrubbing will only remove more paint. At that stage the right move is a proper exterior repaint that starts with a thorough wash and mildew treatment and finishes with two full coats of 100% acrylic.

faqs.q: Can I pressure wash pollen off my house?
faqs.a: Use low pressure only. A soft wash with a house-wash detergent removes pollen without forcing water behind siding or damaging wood and stucco. High-pressure tips can do more harm than the pollen.
Pollen itself is not corrosive, but when it sits on paint it holds moisture, feeds mildew, and leaves a stain that is hard to remove. Regular rinsing prevents most of that.

faqs.q: When is pollen season in North Central Florida?
faqs.a: Oak and pine pollen is heaviest from late winter into spring, typically peaking around February through April depending on the year. Plan a wash once the heaviest drop is over.
Bleach is for mildew, not pollen. A detergent made for exterior house washing is the better choice for pollen. If both are present, use a product labeled for both and protect plants.
